description: und, und-Latn, x-private and en-x-custom loaded together. LocaleUtils.normalizedLanguage returns empty for undetermined and private-use tags, so und and und-Latn create no tiebreaker ambiguity at all (DefaultStrings skips them when grouping loaded locales by language code), while en-x-custom DOES carry primary language en and therefore forces a tiebreaker permutation with en. That asymmetry is the point of the fixture. NOTE (ingest): the und-Latn catalog was REMOVED. Loading both und and und-Latn makes the language 'und' ambiguous, and DefaultStrings then rejects the required tiebreaker entry outright with "Tiebreaker language code 'und' must identify a primary language" — so that catalog set cannot be built at all. und-Latn survives here as a REQUESTED tag, which is what the cases actually exercise.
